properties.description:
crates/reflow2-core/tests/delivery_kind.rs, 10 cases.

WHAT IT PINS: that model work with a passing check reports delivered; that model work WITHOUT a check does not, so the declaration loosens which evidence is required and never whether any is; that an artifact capability still needs both halves; that an UNDECLARED capability keeps the stricter rule, so nothing written before this quietly loosens; that a bad delivery kind is refused naming the legal values; that declaring on an absent capability is refused; and that the setter preserves every other property, which is the BL-183 shape where a sharpening write silently unbuilds a verified capability.

THE TWO THAT EARN THEIR KEEP MOST:

an_unbuilt_capability_with_a_passing_check_is_not_delivered pins THE REJECTED FIX — the version first proposed and first APPROVED, before reading the code showed it was wrong. Inferring `model` from a missing artifact reports unbuilt work as delivered the moment any check is pointed at it, because the commonest reason a capability has no file is that nobody has built it. Without this test the cheaper rule is one refactor away from being reinstated as a simplification.

an_outstanding_item_with_a_check_but_no_file_names_the_remedy pins DISCOVERABILITY, with a sibling asserting the note stays SILENT when there is no check at all. Fixing the rule while leaving the declaration unmentioned would have reproduced, inside the very change that documents it, the failure found four separate times that day: the mechanism exists, is tested, and is unreachable from where the person is stuck.

NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: nothing checks that an author declared the RIGHT kind. That is a judgement about their own work, and reflow2 records what a person knows rather than second-guessing it — the same position REALIZES.conformance takes.
properties.findings:
RUN 2026-08-20: 10 passed, 0 failed. Whole crate 1121 passed / 0 failed across 107 binaries, exactly +10 tests and +1 binary against the 1111/106 baseline — a foundation module and the schema were touched and nothing else moved. Re-run against the FINAL tree after an earlier run overlapped an edit, because a measurement taken around a change is the error this session made twice.

PROVEN ON THE LIVE GRAPH, not only fixtures: both capabilities of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold were declared `model` through the served tool, and the increment went from two `outstanding` to two `delivered`. The discoverability note fired on the real case beforehand and correctly disappeared afterwards.

A DEFECT THIS RUN CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD: inserting the new tool between an existing #[tool(...)] attribute and its function SWAPPED TWO SERVED DESCRIPTIONS — set_interface_designation described capability delivery and set_capability_delivery described interface designation. cargo build, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo fmt and 1121 tests were all clean. Only the toolsnap gate saw it. An attribute is legal Rust wherever it sits; which function a description belongs to is a fact about the SERVED SURFACE, and only a check that reads the served surface can hold it.
